articles.summary: Finance PAYE Tax in Nigeria: An Employer’s Guide Oluwakemi Adesina October 15, 2026 Before your team sees their salary, PAYE tax in Nigeria must be calculated, deducted, and sent on its way to the tax authorities. For business owners and HR teams, this means payroll is never just about paying salaries on time. Every single cycle requires accurate calculations, precise deductions, and timely remittances. This matters even more under Nigeria’s new tax framework. This guide explains what PAYE is, how PAYE is calculated under the 2026 framework, what employers are responsible for, and what they need to keep in place for accurate payroll and tax compliance. What Is PAYE Tax in Nigeria? This is Nigeria’s system of collecting personal income tax from employees at the point of salary payment, through the employer. To clear up a common misconception: the employer does not pay this tax**.** The employee bears the ultimate tax liability, but you; the employer; act as the collection agent. Your job is to calculate it correctly, deduct it from each salary, and remit it to the relevant tax authority. Two things trip up many growing businesses: PAYE is administered by the appropriate tax authority based on the employee’s tax position and applicable jurisdiction, not simply where your company’s head office is registered. PAYE is entirely separate from corporate income tax, VAT, and other business obligations. It lives inside your payroll system, which means accurate employee records are your absolute foundation. Small data errors here compound quietly across every single pay cycle. How Does PAYE Work for Employees? For your team, the journey from gross salary to final take-home pay has three distinct stages: gross income, statutory deductions and reliefs, and tax applied to the resulting taxable income. Let’s look at Amara, who earns a gross annual salary of ₦4,800,000. Before PAYE is calculated, her taxable income is whittled down by statutory deductions and reliefs: Pension (8% of emoluments): ₦384,000 annually NHF (2.5% of basic salary): approximately ₦108,000 annually Rent relief: 20% of annual rent paid (subject to the applicable limits) Because PAYE is calculated against net taxable income, two employees earning the exact same gross pay might take home different amounts depending on their individual reliefs. How Is PAYE Tax Calculated in Nigeria? Under the current personal income tax framework, income is taxed progressively using graduated annual bands after all applicable deductions and reliefs have been applied: Annual Taxable Income Tax Rate Up to ₦800,000 0% (tax-free) ₦800,001 to ₦3,000,000 15% ₦3,000,001 to ₦12,000,000 18% ₦12,000,001 to ₦25,000,000 21% ₦25,000,001 to ₦50,000,000 23% Above ₦50,000,000 25% Keep in mind that these rates are progressive, each band applies only to the slice of income falling within it, rather than your total earnings. Putting It Together: Amara’s Calculation Gross annual income: ₦4,800,000 Less pension (8%): ₦384,000 Less NHF: ₦108,000 Less rent relief: ₦200,000 (20% of ₦1,000,000 annual rent) Taxable income: ₦4,108,000 PAYE calculation: First ₦800,000: ₦0 Next ₦2,200,000 (to ₦3,000,000) at 15%: ₦330,000 Remaining ₦1,108,000 at 18%: ₦199,440 Total annual PAYE: ₦529,440 Monthly PAYE deduction: ₦44,120 Note: Always ensure your finance team is pulling the most up-to-date tax tables What Are an Employer’s PAYE Responsibilities? When it comes to PAYE, the employer owns the entire deduction and remittance chain. Your core duties include: Calculate Accurately: Use current tax bands and proper reliefs for every eligible staff member. Deduct from payroll: Pull the calculated tax out of gross salary before net pay is locked in. **Remit on time:**Ensure deductions reach the right authority like the Nigeria Revenue Service on schedule. Maintain Records: Keep retrievable employee logs, deduction calculations, and remittance receipts. File Annual Returns: Submit your annual returns with the relevant tax authority by January 31st for the preceding tax year. PAYE Filing and Remittance in Nigeria For employers, PAYE remittance is a strict monthly rhythm. The cycle; you run your payroll, compute individual deductions, sum up the total, and remit the exact amount to the relevant tax authority by the 10th day of the following month. If you manage a distributed team spread across different states or tax jurisdictions, you will need to handle separate remittances to the appropriate state or federal authorities. Common PAYE Payroll Mistakes Employers Should Avoid Most PAYE errors are not deliberate. They are the natural output of processes that have not kept pace with changed rules or growing headcount. Outdated tax tables: Relying on old structures instead of current legislative frameworks. Incorrect taxable income: Failing to apply statutory deductions and reliefs consistently before running tax bands. Incorrect tax jurisdiction: Assuming a company’s registered address dictates where PAYE goes, rather than the employee’s actual operational tax position. Missing deadlines: Missing the monthly 10th-day remittance window. Inconsistent records: Discrepancies between what was paid out, what was deducted, and what was filed. Manual processes at scale: Relying on spreadsheets that invite human data-entry errors at scale. PAYE Compliance and Payroll Record Keeping PAYE compliance is not just about getting the number right, it’s also about being able to prove it. Every business should maintain an organised file per employee, per month, capturing: Gross salary and allowances Statutory deductions and reliefs applied Final taxable income and PAYE deducted Net salary paid and official remittance confirmation receipts Maintaining a solid audit trail through proper Payroll Reconciliation and regular Payroll Audit checks ensures your HR and finance teams can respond to queries in minutes. Also, because these files contain sensitive personal data, ensure they are handled in strict alignment with guidelines from the Nigeria Data Protection Commission. Implementing robust Payroll Internal Controls adds an extra layer of defense against accidental discrepancies. How Payroll Software Can Support PAYE Management Technology doesn’t magically make a business tax-compliant, that ultimate responsibility still rests with you. What reliable Payroll Software does do is remove the exhausting manual layers where human error thrives. Modern Payroll Management tools centralise employee data, apply current tax rules automatically, calculate statutory deductions cleanly, and generate ready-to-file records.
